stem:
Uday studies the figure. Lines $p$ and $q$ each carry a single arrow mark. Lines $r$ and $s$ meet with a small square at the meeting point.

Which reading of the marks is correct?

options.text: Call the marks labels only, without saying what parallel or perpendicular relation they show.
Treat the small square as marking any acute angle, skipping that it marks a right angle.
The matching single arrow marks show $p \parallel q$, and the small square shows that $r$ is perpendicular to $s$.
Say that drawing the arrow marks is what creates lines $p$ and $q$.

teacher.key_rationale: Matching arrow counts mark parallel lines; a small square marks a right angle, so those lines are perpendicular. Naming marks as bare labels, reading the square as any acute angle, or reversing marks and lines all miss that notation.
teacher.figure_note: two parallel lines with single arrows; two lines meeting with a right-angle square
